papers.title: "Frontal Slow-Wave Asymmetry in Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Its Modulation During CPAP Titration".
papers.summary: In 143 OSA patients undergoing diagnostic polysomnography followed by CPAP titration, frontal delta power during N3 sleep decreased bilaterally with CPAP (AHI 27.4 to 3.2 events/h), and the absolute interhemispheric slow-wave asymmetry index fell from 9.35% to 7.55%, with dominance shifting from right to left. The authors conclude that respiratory stabilization may modulate cortical slow-wave organization.

papers.title: Characterization of Sleep, Spectral, and Epileptiform Activity in Individuals Aged 8-27 Years with SYNGAP1-Related Disorder Using an at-Home Dry EEG Headband
papers.summary: Using an at-home dry-electrode EEG headband, the study collected 180 multi-night recordings (23 participants) in SYNGAP1-related disorder and found interictal epileptiform discharges in 22 of 23 participants without electrographic seizures, plus increased wake after sleep onset, reduced sleep efficiency, altered N1/N2/N3 staging, and elevated broadband power with reduced relative alpha power and alpha-theta ratio; spectral differences were tightly sleep-stage dependent.

papers.title: Subject-independent classification of ADHD from pediatric EEG: a leakage-aware deep learning framework with interpretable neurophysiological mapping.
papers.summary: Compared classical ML and deep learning models for pediatric ADHD EEG classification under segment-wise versus leakage-free subject-wise cross-validation; SVM on power spectral density features fell from 90.0% to 65.6% accuracy, while a raw-EEG CNN retained 72.7% on unseen participants, with SHAP attributions highlighting frontal (F3, Fz, F4) and central (Cz) electrodes.

papers.title: DINO-EEG: Montage-Robust Event-Level Seizure Detection in Scalp EEG.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: DINO-EEG is a channel-wise framework that predicts seizure onset and offset directly via an object-detection formulation and aggregates channel detections into global events. On TUSZ v2.0.3 under SzCORE, it reached an event-based F1 of 0.641 with mean sensitivity 0.663 at 12.5 false positives per 24 h, remained stable under channel dropout, and transferred to CHB-MIT and Siena without retraining.

papers.title: SOFEx: A Self-Organized Feature Extraction Approach for Detecting Mild Cognitive Impairment and Alzheimer's Disease using EEG Datasets.
papers.summary: The authors developed SOFEx, a self-organized rose-pattern feature-engineering framework for EEG, and applied it to 1,905 segments from 168 participants to classify Alzheimer's disease, mild cognitive impairment, and controls. Under leave-one-subject-out validation, accuracy reached 84.09% with 94.47% recall for AD but only 21.18% for MCI, while leave-one-record-out and participant-grouped 10-fold cross-validation reached 93.65% and 96.38%.

papers.title: Frequency-Resolved Connectivity Graphs for EEG-Based Classification of Alzheimer and Frontotemporal Dementia
papers.summary: The study built frequency-resolved EEG connectivity graphs using coherence, phase locking value, and phase lag index across five bands as multi-dimensional edge features to classify Alzheimer's disease and frontotemporal dementia versus healthy controls. Leave-one-subject-out accuracy was 81.13% for AD vs CN and 76.06% for FTD vs CN with far fewer parameters than DICE-net, and saliency maps implicated occipital/temporal electrodes, alpha-band node features, and theta-band edge features.

papers.title: Artefact-free EEG during temporal interference stimulation reveals phase-specific modulation of the human visual cortex
papers.summary: Develops a front-end analogue low-pass filtering and per-recording artefact verification pipeline to record artefact-free EEG during temporal interference stimulation, then tests phase-specific neuromodulation of the visual cortex in 22 healthy participants. In-phase 15.5 Hz TI increased SSVEP amplitude at 14.5 and 15.5 Hz and shortened response times relative to sham and anti-phase TI.

papers.title: Multi-Metric EEG Connectivity and Graph Analysis Reveal Altered Resting-State Networks in Major Depressive Disorder.
papers.summary: Applied multi-metric resting-state EEG connectivity (coherence, PLV, PLI, mutual information) and graph analysis in 30 MDD participants and 28 controls, reporting predominantly lower theta/alpha connectivity across distributed sensor pairs alongside increased beta mutual-information dependence and lower theta/alpha weighted strength and global efficiency.

papers.title: Acute scalp EEG signatures of anterior thalamic DBS in epilepsy:reproducible gamma power enhancement within an aperiodic spectral-state shift
papers.summary: In five patients with drug-resistant epilepsy recorded across 10 sessions one year apart, the study characterized acute scalp-EEG signatures of cyclic anterior thalamic DBS, finding higher 30-70 Hz gamma power during ON versus within-cycle OFF (median +0.94 dB) in all sessions and lower aperiodic exponent and offset in all sessions, while theta suppression did not survive correction.

papers.title: Functional and Structural Neuroanatomic Correlates of Intraoperative Anesthetic Dose-Adjusted EEG Alpha Power Among Older Surgical Patients
papers.summary: In the ALADDIN prospective cohort of 168 older surgical patients with intraoperative EEG, MRI, and CSF data, lower anesthetic dose-adjusted frontoparietal alpha power was associated with altered default mode, dorsal attention, and salience/ventral attention connectivity, lower left occipitotemporal and superior parietal cortical thickness, and greater postoperative delirium incidence and severity.

papers.title: MSANet: a multi-scale spatiotemporal adaptive network for EEG-based driver fatigue recognition.
papers.summary: Proposed MSANet, a multi-scale spatiotemporal adaptive network with multi-granularity temporal gating, graph-node enhancement, and adaptive classifier gating, for cross-subject EEG driver fatigue recognition, achieving 83.64% accuracy/F1 83.74 on Dataset I and 74.64% accuracy/F1 72.92 on Dataset II.

papers.title: Adaptive local temporal weighting for short-window EEG-based SSVEP recognition using FB-eTRCA.
papers.summary: The authors combined adaptive temporal local weighting (ATLW) with FB-eTRCA to improve short-window SSVEP recognition on the Benchmark and BETA 40-target datasets across 0.2-1.4 s windows. Gains were small and mostly non-significant after Holm correction (e.g., 44.79% vs 44.07% at 0.2 s on Benchmark), with ATLW showing transferability to eTRCA at 0.4 s (+0.86 points).

papers.title: Resting-State EEG Aperiodic Activity and Negative Affective Vulnerability: The Mediating Role of Big Five Personality Traits.
papers.summary: In 164 healthy adults, resting-state EEG aperiodic exponent and offset were estimated and related to Big Five traits, trait anxiety, and trait depression; neuroticism showed the strongest and most widespread positive associations with the aperiodic exponent, and the whole-brain exponent–trait anxiety association became nonsignificant after controlling for personality traits, with significant indirect effects via neuroticism and conscientiousness.

papers.title: The Concise Language Paradigm in left and right hemisphere stroke: a longitudinal source-localized EEG study
papers.summary: Using the Concise Language Paradigm with individualized EEG source reconstruction in left- and right-hemisphere stroke patients assessed at two and seven months, the authors tracked comprehension and production and hemispheric dominance over time. Left-hemisphere patients improved behaviorally and showed systematic shifts from left- to right-hemisphere dominance between sessions, while right-hemisphere patients mainly improved in functional communication.

papers.title: A brain functional network framework based on EEG connectivity for major depressive disorder recognition.
papers.summary: Built multi-frequency resting-state EEG brain functional networks using phase-locking value and Pearson correlation in major depressive disorder, identifying increased left frontal, central, and parietal connectivity in low-frequency bands and altered parietal betweenness centrality in the alpha band; a support vector machine on PLV node features achieved the highest mean balanced accuracy of 81.44% for MDD versus healthy control classification.

papers.title: A brain-behavior generative model links individual brain dynamics to perceptual decisions
papers.summary: Introduces a brain-behavior generative model in which whole-brain dynamics on each participant's structural connectome generate both single-trial EEG and reaction times, fitted to 17 participants performing motion discrimination. The models reproduced individual event-related potentials and reaction-time distributions and predicted held-out trial speed, while in silico silencing showed sensorimotor regions consistently affected decision speed but the same parietal region had opposite effects across participants.

papers.title: EEG Biomarkers for Rett Syndrome: A Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning and Deep Learning with Explainable AI
papers.summary: Compared power-spectral-density machine learning with end-to-end deep learning on resting-state eyes-closed EEG for Rett syndrome classification using subject-wise cross-validation; Random Forest performed best among classical models and EEGNet among deep learning models, and SHAP and occlusion sensitivity both highlighted delta and theta oscillations and centro-frontal regions as key contributors.

papers.title: An attention-enhanced hybrid CNN-BiLSTM framework for multiclass epileptic seizure recognition using EEG signals.
papers.summary: Developed a CNN-BiLSTM-MHSA hybrid deep learning framework for multiclass epileptic seizure recognition on 11,500 EEG segments, reporting 98.83% accuracy, 98.90% F1-score, and 99.80% ROC-AUC and outperforming several recent state-of-the-art EEG seizure classifiers.

papers.title: Decoding motor imagery EEG signals by a deep learning network integrating multiscale filtering and temporal-channel attention mechanisms.
papers.summary: The authors propose a deep learning network for motor-imagery EEG decoding that combines four parallel multiscale CNN branches with Transformer blocks, channel attention fusion, and a CNN classifier, with training-data augmentation. It achieved average accuracies of 80.21%, 90.19%, and 97.32% on three public BCI datasets, exceeding the strongest baselines by 2.59, 1.27, and 1.99 percentage points.

papers.title: EEG Edge-Centric Dynamics Reveal Distinct Post-Stroke Somatosensory Network Responses to Vibratory and Electrical Stimulation.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: Applied edge-centric dynamic connectivity to whole-brain EEG in 15 chronic stroke participants and 15 healthy controls during forearm stimulation, finding that focal vibratory stimulation versus neuromuscular electrical stimulation in stroke produced shorter global theta-network latency, higher contralesional alpha network diversity, and reduced theta-alpha phase-amplitude coupling.

papers.title: Domain-Tailored Attention Transformer for EEG-Based Person Identification.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: Proposes the Domain-Tailored Attention Transformer (DTAT) for EEG-based person identification, with separate spatial (DCT-informed), temporal (amplitude-aware), and spectral (adaptive) attention modules. Reports that DTAT outperforms state-of-the-art methods across multiple EEG datasets.

papers.title: ACF-Net: Design of an adaptive cross-modal fusion network for cross-subject wearable EEG-EMG gesture recognition.
papers.summary: The authors developed ACF-Net, a four-stage EEG-EMG fusion pipeline embedding corticomuscular coherence priors, directed cross-modal attention, SPD manifold embedding, and physiology-consistent test-time adaptation for cross-subject gesture recognition. It reached 87.6% on WAY-EEG-GAL and 89.2% on WEE-Ges, exceeding the strongest baseline by 9.4 and 9.1 percentage points, with ablations attributing gains to directed attention, prior injection, manifold embedding, and adaptation.

papers.title: Reduced neural sensitivity to emotional faces and voices in preterm five-year-olds: a comparative study.
papers.summary: Using frequency-tagging EEG oddball paradigms, this study compared implicit neural discrimination of facial and vocal emotional expressions in 66 preterm five-year-olds and 32 full-term peers. Children born before 32 weeks showed reduced neural sensitivity to facial emotion changes, all preterm children showed reduced sensitivity to vocal changes, and reduced sensitivity to happy expressions was associated with more parent-reported social difficulties.

papers.title: Multimodal Analysis of Brain Network Abnormalities in Autism Spectrum Disorder: a Graph Neural Network-based Fusion Investigation of EEG and fNIRS.
papers.summary: Fuses concurrent EEG and fNIRS data from 58 ASD and 63 typically developing children using graph neural networks to identify autism, achieving 84% accuracy and outperforming single-modality approaches. Graph and topological analyses reveal group differences in motor-language integration, lateralization, and lower average local efficiency in ASD.

papers.title: EEG-Captioner: Grounding EEG-to-Language Generation in Fundamental Signal Properties
papers.summary: Builds an EEG-language dataset of 160,781 segments with signal-level question answering and feature-grounded captions, and introduces a Dual-Domain EEG Encoder and EEG-Captioner framework trained on both QA and caption supervision. The framework achieves 88.81% macro-balanced accuracy on signal-level QA and improves caption factual consistency from 82.06% to 83.46%.

papers.title: EEG-VTSFN: An enhanced approach for differentiating between unipolar and bipolar mood disorders.
papers.summary: Proposed VTSFN, a VAE-based time-space fusion network using LSTM and attention to differentiate bipolar disorder from unipolar depression from EEG, achieving test accuracy 79.3% and AUC 82.7%. In a diagnostic-switch cohort, it identified 17/22 converters (sensitivity 77.3%) and found distinct latent co-activation patterns between groups.

papers.title: Robust acoustic representation of Japanese vowels under phonation variability using dynamic spectral analysis.
papers.summary: Compares static formant descriptors with dynamic Vowel Inherent Spectral Change features for representing Japanese vowels across normal and whispered phonation, using SVM and Random Forest classifiers as analytical probes. Dynamic spectral features yielded more consistent vowel discrimination across phonation types than static-only representations, primarily due to representation properties rather than classifier choice.

papers.title: Localising the Seizure Onset Zone from Routine Interictal and Ictal Scalp EEG Via a Factorised Spatiotemporal Ensemble Deep Learning Framework
papers.summary: Developed a factorised spatiotemporal ensemble deep learning framework to localize the seizure onset zone from routine interictal and ictal scalp EEG in 100 unilateral focal epilepsy patients. The ensemble achieved 88.46% session-level exact match on internal test data (vs 50.00% for EEGNet) and generalized to seizure-free (82.76%) and cross-institutional (84.62%) cohorts, processing a 24-hour recording in 4.26 minutes.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence applications in intracranial electroencephalography for epilepsy management: Insights from AI in Epilepsy 2025.
papers.summary: This review examines artificial intelligence applications to intracranial EEG (including stereo-EEG) for epilepsy management, covering epileptogenic zone localization, surgical outcome prediction, multimodal MRI integration, and optimization of iEEG-guided stimulation and neuromodulation. It reports that current evidence is largely preliminary, dominated by retrospective single-center studies lacking independent external validation, while highlighting multimodal data integration and continuous sensing as promising directions.

papers.title: It's about time: modeling circadian regulation of cardiac electrophysiology and arrhythmogenesis.
papers.journal: American journal of physiology. Cell physiology

papers.title: Hemodynamics, plasma catecholamines, and power spectral analysis of heart rate variability during tilt-evoked neurally mediated hypotension.
keywords: heart rate variability power spectral analysis
papers.summary: In a retrospective comparison of 25 subjects with tilt-evoked neurally mediated hypotension (NMH) and 34 controls, NMH was associated with steeper falls in blood pressure, forearm and systemic vascular resistance, and heart rate variability (HFRR/LFRR), plus greater forearm vasodilation and a larger plasma epinephrine rise without a norepinephrine difference. The authors interpret this as sympathoadrenal imbalance with a precipitous LFRR decline triggering NMH.

papers.title: Clinical and resting-state EEG changes following neurofeedback in adult refugees with persistent trauma-related symptoms: a transdiagnostic pre-post observational study.
papers.summary: In a retrospective pre-post observational study of 53 adult refugees with persistent trauma-related symptoms receiving individualized neurofeedback within multidisciplinary treatment, 62.3% showed clinically meaningful improvement. Resting-state EEG showed increased global alpha amplitude and reduced occipital alpha reactivity, though these changes were not significantly associated with clinical improvement.

papers.title: N-back electroencephalography asymmetry and peripheral immune cell subpopulation composition.
papers.summary: In 24 healthy young adults, this study tested associations between peripheral immune cell subpopulation proportions (estimated via DNA methylation) and EEG asymmetry during a 2-back working memory task. Theta asymmetry was associated with natural killer cell and CD4+ T cell proportions, and immune markers significantly predicted 2-back target accuracy across three regression models, though some correlations did not survive Bonferroni correction.

papers.title: Intracranial EEG for Detecting Epileptic Activity in Acute Brain Injury: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
papers.summary: This PRISMA-guided systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of 12 cohorts (n=864) found that intracranial EEG in acute brain injury detected more seizures/status epilepticus (26% vs 15%) and rhythmic/periodic or ictal-interictal patterns (47% vs 34%) than surface EEG, with no severe adverse events reported. Pooled paired analyses showed additional iEEG-only detection in 16.5% for seizures and 26% for rhythmic/periodic patterns, though these paired odds ratios were not statistically significant.

papers.title: Glycosides of Cistanche improve cognitive dysfunction in sleep-deprived model rats by activating the SIRT1/PGC-1α/Nrf2 signaling pathway.
papers.summary: In sleep-deprived rats, glycosides of Cistanche improved Morris water maze performance, reduced oxidative stress (lower MDA, higher GSH-Px and SOD), and attenuated hippocampal CA1 neuronal and mitochondrial damage while upregulating SIRT1/PGC-1α/Nrf2 pathway and synaptic proteins; the protective effects were abolished by the SIRT1 inhibitor EX527.

papers.title: Behavioural expression of ictal embarrassment: a stereo-EEG case report.
papers.summary: This stereo-EEG case report describes a 40-year-old woman with drug-resistant focal epilepsy whose ictal embarrassment arose from seizure onset in the middle frontal gyrus bank of the superior frontal sulcus (F2sb) with propagation to dorsal anterior cingulate cortex and superior anterior insula. Electrical stimulation reproduced the seizure, but the full behavioral embarrassment repertoire emerged only in the standing position and was associated with reduced node strength in a frontal-cingulo-insular network, suggesting bodily context shapes its expression.

papers.title: Perioperative Neurocognitive Disorders in Older Adults: Mechanisms, Biomarkers, and Evidence-Informed Management.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes mechanisms (neuroinflammation, blood-brain barrier dysfunction, neurotransmitter imbalance, oxidative stress, synaptic dysfunction), candidate fluid biomarkers and EEG features, and evidence-informed management of perioperative neurocognitive disorders in older adults undergoing cardiac and noncardiac surgery. It concludes that multicomponent prevention and individualized anesthetic care remain most defensible, while EEG-guided titration, biomarkers, and machine-learning tools are promising but not yet replacement for standardized clinical assessment.

papers.title: [Discussion on the closed-loop regulation strategy for acupuncture "Deqi" based on brain-computer interface and its peripheral-central mechanisms].
papers.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
papers.summary: This review proposes a brain-computer interface-based closed-loop strategy for objectively identifying and actively maintaining the acupuncture "Deqi" state, synthesizing evidence that EEG can capture millisecond-scale neural oscillation dynamics during Deqi and discussing peripheral-central mechanisms and current technical challenges.

papers.title: KAT6A-Mutant iPSC-Derived Cortical Neurons Display Precocious Maturation, Dysregulated Electrophysiology, and Altered Morphology.
papers.summary: Using KAT6A syndrome patient-derived iPSC cortical neurons, this study found altered transcriptomes enriched for autism spectrum disorder-related genes, early hyperexcitability followed by later hypoexcitability with reduced sodium and potassium currents, fewer GABA-positive neurons, increased spontaneous calcium activity, and morphometric signs of precocious maturation. KAT6A knockout SH-SY5Y cells also showed impaired differentiation and dysregulated gene expression.

papers.title: GABAergic subiculum-medial entorhinal projection in mice and rats.
papers.summary: Using enhancer-driven AAV labeling and anterograde tracing in mice and rats, this study identified a conserved GABAergic inhibitory projection from dorsal subiculum to dorsal medial entorhinal cortex, enriched in superficial MEC layers, forming inhibitory synapses and partly arising from parvalbumin-positive neurons. This extends the canonical view of subicular output as excitatory.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
